# Outstanding work

Where the open work is, by the only division the repository actually encodes: whether an issue names a machine.

## Cross-cutting work

[Open issues carrying no `system:` label](https://github.com/emu198x/emu198x/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+-label%3Asystem%3Aatom+-label%3Asystem%3Abbc-micro+-label%3Asystem%3Aelectron+-label%3Asystem%3Acpc+-label%3Asystem%3Aatari-2600+-label%3Asystem%3Aatari-5200+-label%3Asystem%3Aatari-7800+-label%3Asystem%3Aatari-800xl+-label%3Asystem%3Acolecovision+-label%3Asystem%3Aamiga+-label%3Asystem%3Ac64+-label%3Asystem%3Apet+-label%3Asystem%3Avic-20+-label%3Asystem%3Adragon+-label%3Asystem%3Ajupiter-ace+-label%3Asystem%3Aaquarius+-label%3Asystem%3Amtx+-label%3Asystem%3Amsx+-label%3Asystem%3Agame-boy+-label%3Asystem%3Anes+-label%3Asystem%3Aoric+-label%3Asystem%3Agame-gear+-label%3Asystem%3Amaster-system+-label%3Asystem%3Asg-1000+-label%3Asystem%3Aspectrum+-label%3Asystem%3Azx80+-label%3Asystem%3Azx81+-label%3Asystem%3Asord-m5+-label%3Asystem%3Asvi-328+-label%3Asystem%3Aeinstein) — shared infrastructure, CPU and chip crates, tooling, release plumbing, and anything spanning several machines. ## What this page does not do

**It does not rank machines.** Nothing committed to this repository encodes priority — not the registry, not the dependency graph, not the labels. Ordering the table by anything but machine name would be inventing a claim and presenting it as derived. Roadmap order lives in `RULES.md` and the decision records, where it is stated by a person and can be argued with.

**It does not list issue counts.** They change hourly. Every link above is a live query, which is both current and honest about being fetched rather than remembered.
